content:
Here's a translation of the Greek text:

And then the lord of men Agamemnon addressed him:

"'185 I rejoice, son of Laertes, hearing your word,
for in due measure you have reached and recounted everything.
And these things I too wish to swear, and my heart urges me,
nor will I swear falsely towards a god. But let Achilles
remain there, eager as he is for war.
190And all you others, remain together, so that the gifts
may come from the huts and we may cut the oaths that are trustworthy.
And to you yourself, I give this command and order:
having chosen the best of the young men of the Achaeans,
to carry the gifts from my ship, all that we promised to give Achilles
195yesterday, and to lead the women.
And let Talthybius quickly through the wide army of the Achaeans
prepare a boar to sacrifice to Zeus and to Hēlios."
